speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your episodes of unresponsiveness and facial grimacing, can you describe what typically happens right before an episode starts?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed description. Do you have any history of febrile seizures, head trauma, or a family history of epilepsy?

speaker: Doctor
text: The muddy taste you described is a very specific aura that often points to seizures originating in the temporal lobe. Do the episodes tend to happen at a particular time of day, such as upon waking or at night?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Doctor

The clinical picture of a focal aware seizure evolving to impaired awareness with a gustatory aura is highly suggestive of temporal lobe epilepsy, so I need to confirm epileptiform activity. I will also check for any structural abnormalities that might be causing these seizures.

The EEG findings of right temporal interictal spikes strongly correlate with the patient's gustatory aura and behavioral arrest. Given the clinical presentation and electrographic evidence, I have reached a conclusion.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
